A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same XYZ-IBD dataset and annotation pipeline. Their text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. v1's supplementary Sections A–C were compared against the complete v3 PDF, allowing relocated material to be distinguished from omissions.

before.justification: v1 reports original annotation-error simulations and experimental results for object detection, 6D pose estimation, and monocular depth estimation, including Tables 4–6.

after.justification: v3 retains the original annotation-error evaluation and reports detection and pose-estimation experiments in Table 4, supplemented by dataset statistics and qualitative predictions.

M1.justification: The collection and annotation procedure remains unchanged: calibrated viewpoints, anti-reflection coating, multi-view depth fusion, manual CAD alignment, multi-scale ICP, and pose propagation. Simulation-based error quantification also retains the same procedure. Added baseline evaluations do not introduce a new proposed method.

E1.justification: v3 adds explicit performance comparisons across YCB-V, T-LESS, LM-O, IC-BIN, and TUD-L, whereas v1's benchmark results concern XYZ-IBD. Conversely, v1's monocular-depth evaluation and TRICKY task disappear. The underlying XYZ-IBD objects, scenes, and synthetic training coverage remain substantially unchanged.

E2.justification: v3 Table 4 adds NIDS-Net for unseen-object 2D detection and MatchU for unseen-object 6D detection. The earlier 2D/6D comparators remain, including GDRNet renamed GDRN in the table and SAM-6D under varying labels. Depth Anything V2 disappears with the depth evaluation.

E3.justification: v3 adds an average AP across five BOP datasets and removes the depth-specific scale/shift alignment, material-subset evaluation, and depth metrics. The retained 2D IoU-based AP, 6D MSSD/MSPD-based AP, detection-mask priors, and synthetic-training/real-testing design remain unchanged. The relocated split description does not establish a changed XYZ-IBD split.

E4.justification: v3 adds validation/test scene-density histograms in Figure 9 and qualitative detection/pose comparisons in Figure 10, including examples of incorrect object identities. The cross-dataset instance-distribution analysis already existed in v1 Appendix C and is relocated to v3 Figure 4. Annotation validation and noise-sensitivity analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report annotation errors of 0.999 mm with standard deviation 0.12 mm and 0.432 degrees with standard deviation 0.08 degrees, using the same stated simulation sampling. Neither adds baseline run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Relabeling the existing instance-statistics chart does not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Between v1 Table 5 and v3 Table 4, reported XYZ-IBD 6D AP changes from 0.274 to 0.247 for SurfEmb, 0.547 to 0.564 for FoundationPose, and 0.438 to 0.578 for SAM-6D. The leading method consequently changes from FoundationPose to SAM-6D. v3 also adds cross-dataset results and NIDS-Net/MatchU entries, while removing depth results. The PDFs do not explain whether the revised shared scores reflect corrections or reruns.

T1.justification: The MSSD, MSPD, and AP equations are retained without substantive mathematical revision. Neither version introduces additional theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations. Removing the depth-metric explanation changes evaluation documentation rather than theoretical content.

C1.justification: v3 narrows the advertised benchmarking contribution from detection, pose estimation, and depth estimation to 2D/6D detection. The central claims concerning industrial complexity, accurate annotations, and difficulty relative to household benchmarks remain. Sub-millimeter accuracy receives greater prominence, but v1 already claimed accuracy below 1 mm.

C2.justification: v3 newly interprets YOLOX's comparable cross-dataset performance as occurring under an 'overfitting setup.' Its conclusion replaces v1's explicit warning about working-distance and object-scale limits on generalization to other materials and shapes with a broader future-expansion statement. The depth-specific interpretation of insufficient industrial precision is also removed.

D1.justification: v3 omits v1 Appendix B's batch sizes, training budgets, GPU specifications, and runtimes for YOLOX, GDRNet, and SurfEmb. It also omits the detailed five-view selection instructions, direct download/evaluation/toolkit links, and dataset directory diagram. Some split information moves into Section 4.1, which additionally specifies frame counts and 10–60 simulated instances; these disclosures do not establish changed experimental settings.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations and discussion for MatchU, NIDS-Net, and Grounding DINO, while removing Depth Anything V2, GDRNPP, and some depth-benchmark references. The household-versus-industrial dataset positioning and most of Section 2 remain unchanged. The introduction adds criticism of measurement biases in existing industrial ground truth.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Benchmark sections are reorganized around dataset splits and seen/unseen tasks, selected supplementary material moves into the main text, and the separate supplement disappears. Author information changes and an acknowledgements section is added. These are extensive narrative and structural revisions despite the stable annotation method.

P2.justification: v3 substantially reworks page layout and figure placement, expands and transposes the benchmark table into cross-dataset comparisons, revises sample montages, and adds split histograms and qualitative prediction grids. The depth tables and directory diagram disappear. Existing CAD and pipeline illustrations are retained or relocated, while the instance-statistics chart moves from v1 Figure 9 to v3 Figure 4 with revised legend labels.

improvement.justification: v3 Table 4 provides direct cross-dataset evidence for the central industrial-difficulty claim, and the qualitative comparisons make failures easier to assess. However, removing v1's baseline training recipes and practical evaluation guidance materially reduces reproducibility, while the limitations become less explicit. The changed shared-method scores are also unexplained. These substantive gains and losses leave the net effect on overall paper quality uncertain.
